questions.question: Interview: string indexing ke rules batao — 0-based, negative indexing aur out-of-range behaviour.
questions.answer:
· Index 0 se shuru, last index `len(s) - 1`.
· Negative: `s[-1]` last character, `s[-len(s)]` pehla. Verified: `'abc'[-1]` → c, `'abc'[-len('abc')]` → a.
· Bahar nikalne par IndexError: `'abc'[-4]` → IndexError: string index out of range, aur `'abc'[3]` bhi same.
· Slice me ye strictness NAHI hai: `'abc'[-4:]` → 'abc' (clamp ho jata hai).

Rule yaad rakho: index par IndexError, slice par clamp — isliye safe extraction ke liye slice use karo.
questions.explanation: Interview me `-len(s)` bound aur index-vs-slice error behaviour — ye do points clarity dikhate hain.

questions.question: Interview: slicing ka poora syntax `s[start:stop:step]` samjhao — defaults aur out-of-range behaviour ke saath.
questions.answer:
Verified:

s = 'Python'
print(repr(s[100:200]), repr(s[-100:]), len(s[100:200]), s[2:100])
# '' 'Python' 0 thon

· `start` default 0, `stop` default len(s), `step` default 1.
· `stop` EXCLUSIVE hai: `s[0:3]` → 'Pyt' (3 characters).
· Out-of-range indices clamp ho jate hain — kabhi IndexError nahi: `s[100:200]` → '' (khaali string), `s[-100:]` → poori string, `s[2:100]` → 'thon'.
· Khaali slice valid hai: `'abc'[1:1]` → ''.
questions.explanation: Interview me "slicing never raises IndexError, it clamps" — ye line confidence dikhati hai, aur defensive code me slices prefer karne ki wajah bhi.

questions.question: Interview: step slicing ke practical use-cases batao — `[::2]`, `[::-1]`, `[::-2]`.
questions.answer:
Verified (s = 'Python'):

print(s[::2], s[1::2], s[::-2], s[2:5:2], s[::-1])
# Pto yhn nhy to nohtyP

· `[::2]` → alternate characters (index 0, 2, 4) — sampling, every-other-char
· `[1::2]` → odd indices
· `[::-1]` → reversed string (negative step left se chalta hai)
· `[::-2]` → reverse + alternate (nhy)
· `[2:5:2]` → 'to' — step ke saath start/stop bhi lagta hai

Negative step ka matlab: start default becomes len-1 aur stop default -1 ki taraf — isliye `s[::-1]` poora reverse deta hai.
questions.explanation: Reverse one-liner (`s[::-1]`) palindrome check me use hota hai — `s == s[::-1]` bina loop.

questions.question: Interview: string immutability ka practical matlab kya hai? `s += 'x'` karne par kya hota hai?
questions.answer:
String ke characters badle nahi ja sakte. Verified:

s = 'hello'
print(id(s))
s += '!'
print(s, id(s))
# hello! <naya id>     ← naya object bana
try: s[0] = 'H'
except TypeError as e: print(e)
# TypeError: 'str' object does not support item assignment

Isliye har `+=` naya string object banata hai. Loop me accumulate karna O(n²) ho jata hai — behtar hai list me parts jama karke `''.join(parts)` (O(n)).

Note: `+` sirf str + str par chalta hai — `'a' + 1` → TypeError: can only concatenate str (not "int") to str.
questions.explanation: Interview me "immutability gives hashability + thread-safety, cost is O(n²) concatenation" — dono side bolo. Id change dikhana strong proof hai.

questions.question: Interview: concatenation (`+`, `*`) aur `join()` me kaun kab use karte hain?
questions.answer:
Verified:

print('-'.join(['a', 'b']), 'a' + 'b')     # a-b ab
print('ab' * 3, repr('ab' * 0), [0] * 3)    # ababab '' [0, 0, 0]

· `+` — do-teen pieces ke liye readable: `greeting + ', ' + name`.
· `*` — repetition: `'=' * 40` (separator), `[0] * n` (initialize list). Zero ya negative multiplier khaali result deta hai.
· `join()` — 2+ elements ki list ke liye: ek hi allocation, fast (O(n)), aur separator control. Loop me `+` se build karna O(n²) hai.

Rule: fixed 2-3 pieces → `+`; list/loop se banaya gaya text → `join`.
questions.explanation: Interview me complexity bolna scoring hai: join O(n) single pass, repeated `+` O(n²).

questions.question: Interview: `len()` exactly kya count karta hai — characters, bytes ya graphemes?
questions.answer:
`len()` Unicode CODE POINTS ginta hai — bytes nahi, aur visible characters (graphemes) bhi nahi. Verified:

print(len('नमस्ते'), len('👍'), len('e' + chr(0x301)), len('é'))
# 6 1 2 1

· 'नमस्ते' → 6 code points (matras/alag akshar alag gine jate hain), bytes me 18 (UTF-8).
· '👍' → 1 (Python 3 me poori emoji ek code point), par display width 2 columns hoti hai.
· 'é' composed (U+00E9) → 1, par 'e' + combining accent (U+0301) → 2 — same dikhta hai, length alag!

Bytes chahiye to `len(s.encode('utf-8'))`; user-visible characters chahiye to `unicodedata`/grapheme library.
questions.explanation: Interview me teen level ka farq bolo: bytes < code points (len) < graphemes (display). Input validation/limits me yahi galti hoti hai.

questions.question: Interview: escape characters kaun kaun se hain aur kab kaam aate hain?
questions.answer:
Verified:

print('a\tb')      # tab (1 character, len('a\tb') == 3)
print('a\nb')      # newline (count 1)
print('c\\d')      # c\d — literal backslash (backslash khud escape hota hai)
print('\x41')     # A  — hex escape
print('\u00e9')   # é  — unicode escape (len 1)

List: `\n` newline, `\t` tab, `\\` backslash, `\'` / `\"` quotes, `\r` carriage return, `\xNN` hex, `\uXXXX`/`\UXXXXXXXX` unicode.

Use: formatted console output, CSV/TSV separators, logs. Windows paths aur regex me escape se bachne ke liye raw string (`r'...'`) use karo.
questions.explanation: Interview me ek real case do: `'C:\new\file'` me `\n` newline ban jata hai — ye silent bug hai.

questions.question: Interview: raw strings (`r'...'`) kya karti hain, aur kab zaroori hoti hain?
questions.answer:
Raw string me backslash ko special treat NAHI kiya jata — jo likha hai wahi milta hai. Verified:

print(repr(r'\n'), len(r'\n'), len('\n'))
# '\\n' 2 1
print(repr(r'C:\new\file'))
# 'C:\\new\\file'

· `r'\n'` → 2 characters (backslash + n), normal `'\n'` → 1 character (newline).
· Raw strings Windows paths (`r'C:\Users\me'`) aur regex (`re.compile(r'\d+')`) ke liye standard hain.
· Limitation: raw string backslash par END nahi ho sakti — `r'\'` → SyntaxError: unterminated string literal.
questions.explanation: Interview me ye nuance bolo: "raw strings still cannot end with an odd number of backslashes, because the backslash would escape the closing quote."

questions.question: Interview: string ko loop kaise karte hain — index ke saath aur bina? `in` operator aur iteration me farq?
questions.answer:
Verified:

for i, ch in enumerate('ab'): print(i, ch)
# 0 a
# 1 b
print(list(reversed('abc')), list('abc'))
# ['c', 'b', 'a'] ['a', 'b', 'c']
print('' in 'abc', 'cb' in 'abc', 'th' in 'python')
# True False True

· `for ch in s:` — characters
· `for i, ch in enumerate(s):` — index + character (manual counter se behtar)
· `reversed(s)` — ulta iterator (naya string nahi banata; `s[::-1]` naya string deta hai)
· `in` — SUBSTRING check karta hai, character-only nahi: `'th' in 'python'` → True
· Edge: khaali string har string ka substring hai — `'' in 'abc'` → True (iss test se hamesha bach ke check karne ka faayda kam hai)
questions.explanation: Interview detail: `in` substring search karta hai aur khaali string ke liye True deta hai — validation code me ye surprise banata hai.

questions.question: Interview: strings compare kaise hote hain? `'Z' < 'a'` True kyun, aur case-insensitive comparison kaise karein?
questions.answer:
Verified:

print('Z' < 'a', 'apple' < 'banana', 'Apple'.lower() == 'apple')
# True True True

· Comparison code point by code point hoti hai (lexicographic): 'Z' (90) < 'a' (97) — isliye uppercase letters chhote letters se pehle aate hain.
· Prefix chhota hota hai: 'app' < 'apple'.
· Case-insensitive: dono ko `lower()`/`upper()` karo ya `casefold()` (Unicode-safe): `'Apple'.casefold() == 'apple'.casefold()` → True.

Sorting ke liye: `sorted(names, key=str.lower)` — warna 'Zebra' 'apple' se pehle aa jayega.
questions.explanation: Interview me ASCII ordering ka trap + casefold vs lower ka farq bolo, aur sorting me key= ka istemaal mention karo.

questions.question: Bug fix karo: `if answer == 'yes' or 'Yes':` har case me True ho jata hai, chahe answer 'no' ho. Kyun, aur sahi check kya hai?
questions.answer:
Reason: `or 'Yes'` ek non-empty string hai → hamesha truthy. Condition `(answer == 'yes') or 'Yes'` ban jati hai, aur 'Yes' sach hai — isliye branch hamesha chalti hai.

answer = 'no'
print(answer == 'yes' or 'Yes')     # Yes      ← truthy!
print(answer.lower() in ('yes', 'y'))   # False  ← sahi check

Fix:
if answer.lower() in ('yes', 'y'):
    ...

Rule: har operand ko apna comparison do — `x == a or x == b` ya `x in (a, b)`.
questions.explanation: Ye beginner-to-intermediate ka classic silent bug hai (koi exception nahi, sirf galat branch). `in` tuple ya `.lower()` normalization fix hai.

questions.question: Bug fix karo: `path = 'C:\new\file'` likha, par path toot gaya (newline aur formfeed ban gaye). Sahi tarika kya hai?
questions.answer:
Problem: `\n` newline banta hai aur `\f` formfeed — Windows path ka structure hi badal jata hai.

bad = 'C:\new\file'
print(repr(bad), len(bad))
# 'C:\\new\x0cile' 9      ← \n aur \f escape ho gaye

good = r'C:\new\file'

questions.question: Checkpoint (self-grade): indexing aur slicing ke poore rules batao — error behaviour ke saath.
questions.answer:
1) Indexing 0-based; negative index end se (`s[-1]` last, `s[-len(s)]` pehla).

2) Out-of-range INDEX → IndexError: string index out of range. Out-of-range SLICE → clamp, koi error nahi: `s[100:200]` → '', `s[-100:]` → poori string, `'abc'[3:]` → ''.

3) Slice syntax `s[start:stop:step]`: start default 0, stop default len(s), step default 1; stop EXCLUSIVE (`s[0:3]` → 3 characters 'Pyt').

4) Step: `s[::2]` → 'Pto', `s[::-1]` → reverse, `s[::-2]` → reverse alternate, `s[2:5:2]` → 'to'.

5) Khaali slice valid: `'abc'[1:1]` → ''. Safe extraction pattern: `s[-1:]` (index nahi).
questions.explanation: Self-grade: index-vs-slice error behaviour aur stop exclusive — ye do rules poore string code me apply hote hain.

questions.question: Checkpoint (self-grade): immutability aur string banane ke operations — kya mutate nahi hota, aur performance ka niyam kya hai?
questions.answer:
1) Strings immutable: `s[0] = 'H'` → TypeError: 'str' object does not support item assignment. Koi bhi 'change' naya string deta hai.

2) `s += 'x'` naam ko naye object par rebind karta hai (id badal jata hai) — purana object untouched.

3) Concatenation: `+` sirf str + str par (`'a' + 1` → TypeError: can only concatenate str (not "int") to str). Repetition `'ab' * 3` → ababab, `* 0`/negative → ''.

4) Performance: loop me `+=` O(n²) (har baar copy) vs `''.join(parts)` O(n). List/loop se text banao → join.

5) Faayda: immutability ki wajah se strings hashable hain (dict keys) aur safely share hoti hain.
questions.explanation: Self-grade: agar tum text ko loop me `+=` se banate ho, to ye checkpoint fail hai — join pe shift karo.

questions.question: Checkpoint (self-grade): text handling ke essentials — len, escapes, raw strings, iteration aur comparison.

1) `len()` code points ginta hai, bytes nahi: 'नमस्ते' → 6 (bytes 18), '👍' → 1, 'e'+combining accent → 2. Bytes → `len(s.encode('utf-8'))`.

2) Escapes: `\n \t \\ \' \" \x41 \u00e9`; `\t`/`\x41` ek character hain (length count me 1).

3) Raw strings: `r'\n'` → 2 characters (backslash + n), normal `'\n'` → 1. Windows paths (`r'C:\new\file'`) aur regex ke liye; backslash par end nahi ho sakti (SyntaxError).

4) Iteration: `for ch in s`, `enumerate(s)` index ke saath, `reversed(s)` iterator; `in` SUBSTRING check hai aur `'' in s` → True (edge case).

5) Comparison: code point order se ('Z' < 'a', prefix chhota); case-insensitive compare → `lower()`/`casefold()`; sort → `key=str.lower`.
questions.explanation: Self-grade: `len` par Unicode ka point aur `r''` ka use-case bina dekhe bata pao to strings section solid hai.
